cells.tense: Here, with the pen, the strength to hold and carry something is present and steady.
cells.act: hold space for what someone feels without fixing it
cells.ask: Next time someone near you is upset, stay with what they feel and leave the solving alone. Offer nothing to fix it. Be there while it's hard; they can walk out with it still messy.
cells.core:
You can stand and carry weight — yours, and what belongs to the people close to you — without having to make it lighter to prove you can. What you hold stays held, and things hold around you. That's steady, and it's working.

What's growing alongside it is staying with someone's feeling instead of steering it. Not fixing. Letting it be real and standing next to it, the way you'd stand beside someone carrying something heavy. You can do that without taking it from them. That's the part worth feeding here: presence that doesn't need the feeling to be finished before it counts for anything.
cells.sheetLine: You carry what's heavy without it having to get lighter first.
cells.verb: building something that holds and carries weight
cells.place: the ground you stand on and can bear staying on

cells.tense: Later, the hand that holds will be bracing against a load it has already decided is coming.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: Before any call you make on someone's behalf, put both sides down — what it costs them and what it gives them — and read it before you decide. If it still holds up, act.
cells.core:
You hold things. That's the gift — and because your body knows what it can stand under, part of you starts standing before anything lands. Holding turns into bracing: a call you might make tomorrow gets weighed today, and the people being held start to feel held a little too hard.

What you can carry is real; what's ahead isn't written yet. Fairness without the counting is what's available here. Before any decision made on someone's behalf, put both sides of it down — what it costs them and what it gives them. If it holds up when you read it back, make the call. If it doesn't, you don't have to.

cells.tense: Back there, the grip on something stayed after the thing itself was done.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Unwrite one reminder you still act on for a thing that's already over or out of your reach. Take it off the list. Leave the space empty and see what your days do with it.
cells.core:
Standing here, you keep hold of something you can't carry forward. The hands are still closed around it, and the part of you built to take on what's next has gone quiet behind that grip. It isn't hardness. It's grip that didn't get the message.

What opens this isn't trying harder — that's the trap. It's letting one thing be finished. Unwrite one reminder you still act on for something that's over or out of your reach. Take it off the list and leave the space empty. Don't fill it with something else. Hold one less thing and notice what your days become with the room it leaves. Enduring comes back when a hand is finally empty.

cells.tense: The strength is here and in use right now, steering people and plans, while the one doing it says nothing of theirs is in it.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Start one thing this week because you want to watch it start. Not because anyone needs it. Something small enough to keep or drop, and tell no one your reason.
cells.core:
You hold things together — it's in your body, in the way you walk into a room and it settles. People move through what you keep standing, and by your own account you had little to do with any of it. The building is yours. The story about it isn't.

There's a simpler form of the same strength underneath all of it: making something because the making is the point. Start one thing because you want to watch it begin — not as a fix for anyone, not something anyone asked for. Keep it or drop it. Say nothing about why. You'll know you did it, and that's the part that has been going unfed.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding it all and saying it isn't yours.
